title: 1. The Hook: The Mystery of the Sleeping Seed
text: Imagine a small Bajra (pearl millet) seed that has been sleeping in a beautifully carved wooden box since 1940. It remembers a time when fields were a festival of colors—different crops growing together, farmers singing during the harvest, and the sweet smell of fresh earth. But today, when it looks out, the fields look empty and smell of chemicals. Why is the little seed sad? What happened to the beautiful farms of the past?

content.title: 2. Socratic Thinking: The Farmer's Choice
content.text: Imagine you are a farmer. You have a big field. Would you rather grow 10 different types of crops (like wheat, bajra, vegetables, and cotton) every year, or just 1 type of crop (like cotton) that makes you the most money? Think about what would happen to the soil if it eats the same 'food' from that one crop every single year!

content.title: 3. Discovery: The Soil's Diet
content.description: Just like we need a balanced diet of roti, dal, sabzi, and fruits, the soil also needs different crops to stay healthy. This is called Crop Rotation.

title: 4. The Reveal: Traditional vs. Modern Farming
text:
In the past, farmers practiced **Traditional Farming**. They used natural fertilizers like cow dung, grew different crops (mixed farming), and stored the best seeds for the next year in wooden boxes protected by neem leaves. 

Then came **Modern Farming**. Farmers started using tractors, electric pumps for water, and chemical fertilizers. Many started growing only one cash crop (like cotton) repeatedly, which is called **Monoculture**. While it gave more money quickly, the chemicals made the soil weak and killed friendly insects like earthworms.

content.definition: The practice of growing only one type of crop in a field year after year, which can make the soil weak.
Factory-made chemicals added to soil to help plants grow faster, but which can harm the soil's natural health over time.

content.title: Wait, aren't chemicals good for plants?
content.text: A common mistake is thinking that chemical fertilizers are food for plants. They are more like 'energy drinks'. They give a quick boost, but if you only drink energy drinks and eat no real food, you become weak. Over time, chemicals make the soil completely barren!

question: Why did farmers traditionally keep neem leaves in the wooden boxes where they stored seeds?
options: To give the seeds a good smell
To protect the seeds from harmful insects
To help the seeds grow faster in the box
To change the color of the seeds

content.title: 6. Reflection: The Farmer's Best Friend
content.text: Earthworms are called the farmer's best friends because they dig tunnels in the soil, making it soft and airy. They also eat dead leaves and turn them into natural fertilizer. Reflect on this: What happens to these helpful earthworms when a farmer sprays harsh chemical medicines on the field?

content.title: 7. Connection: Food and Our Health
content.text: Think about the food on your plate! When fields become weak from too many chemicals, the vegetables and grains grown in them also have fewer vitamins. Traditional farming not only kept the soil healthy but also gave us stronger, healthier food.

content.title: 8. Mastery Challenge: Design Your Organic Farm
content.text: You are starting a new farm that uses only natural methods. List 3 things you will do to keep your soil healthy and protect your seeds without using factory-made chemicals. (Hint: Think about what to mix in the soil, what leaves to use, and how many crops to grow!)
